newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil unsure if economy overheating - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Brazil unsure if economy overheating - ministry.

text.p: The Brazilian Finance Ministry Wednesday said it was impossible to state definitively whether or not the economy was growing at too rapid a rate in late 1996 and early 1997.

"With the information available to date (February 24), it's still not possible to affirm unequivocally whether the economy is on a trajectory of excessive heating up," the ministry said in its monthly report on the economy.
The ministry said the recovery begun in 1996 was based on credit and "does not show an unsustainable trajectory in the short-term".
It said better credit conditions in 1996 -- principally lower interest rates and longer maturities -- had stimulated sales of durable and semi-durable goods.
Physical sales of durables in Sao Paulo rose 13.7 percent in 1996 over 1995 and semi-durable sales increased 11.1 percent, it said.
The report added that latest credit data showed "extremely sharp" year-on-year rises, even in seasonally-adjusted terms.
In January, credit enquiries soared, but the Finance Ministry noted that this could have a lot to do with retailers' promotions.

"The behaviour of industrial production could suggest an acceleration in industrial activity in the second half of (last) year and potentially represent a heating up of the economy," it wrote. "Everything depends on demand, which is intimately connected to credit."
The other side of the credit coin -- bad debt -- had also shown increases in the past few months, the ministry said.
It said the latest estimates for January showed that of every 1,000 checks written, 5.1 bounced, a number only exceeded in June 1995 when 5.2 of every 1,000 checks bounced.
